skill.name: modal
skill.description: Use Modal to design, deploy, and operate serverless Python workloads with GPUs, autoscaling, volumes, secrets, web endpoints, and scheduled jobs.
skill.summary: Guides Modal cloud deployment for Python, ML, GPU, batch, API, and scheduled workloads.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, Modal API examples, placeholder URLs, and documented secret usage. Confirmed issues are limited to unsafe documentation patterns: copying an AWS credential directory, serving a container root path through a shell-launched web server, printing secret-derived environment values, and showing an inline API key placeholder.

remediation.issue: Credential directory copied into a container example
remediation.suggestion: Replace the .aws directory copy example with a non-secret sample directory and recommend Modal Secrets for cloud credentials.

remediation.issue: Web endpoint example launches a shell server for the container root path
remediation.suggestion: Use an ASGI or FastAPI example, avoid shell=True, and serve only a dedicated application directory.

remediation.issue: Secret examples print or inline secret-like values
remediation.suggestion: Avoid printing secret-derived environment variables and show loading API keys from existing Modal Secrets or local environment variables.

content.value_statement: Cloud Python workloads need clear deployment, scaling, and secret patterns. This skill guides Modal apps for GPUs, APIs, batches, volumes, and schedules.
actual_capabilities: Explains Modal authentication, token setup, and first app workflows.
Shows how to define container images with Python packages and system packages.
Guides functions, classes, GPU selection, resources, autoscaling, and parallel maps.
Documents Modal volumes, secrets, web endpoints, and scheduled jobs.
Provides scientific computing examples for ML inference, batch work, and simulations.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include executable helper scripts.
Users need a Modal account and must manage cloud billing.
Examples may need changes for project dependencies, data paths, and permissions.
It does not replace Modal official security, pricing, or API documentation.

use_cases.title: Deploy GPU Inference
use_cases.description: Plan a Modal app that loads a model, requests GPUs, and serves predictions through a web endpoint.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Data Jobs
use_cases.description: Convert local Python batch work into Modal functions that map across inputs and persist outputs.

use_cases.title: Operate Scheduled Cloud Tasks
use_cases.description: Design recurring Modal jobs with secrets, volumes, resource limits, and monitoring expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Modal App
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a simple Modal app for a Python function. Include setup steps, authentication checks, and how to run it locally.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Modal web endpoint for my Python prediction function. Include image dependencies, request handling, deployment steps, and authentication considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Scale a Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my batch data workflow into Modal functions. Recommend map usage, CPU and memory settings, volumes, retries, and cost controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Modal Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Modal architecture for GPU inference, secrets, volumes, autoscaling, and scheduled jobs. Identify reliability, security, and cost risks.

output_examples.input: I need to serve a transformer model with a GPU.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan with image dependencies, GPU choice, model loading flow, endpoint design, and cost guardrails.

output_examples.input: I have thousands of files to process in parallel.
output_examples.output: A batch strategy covering function boundaries, parallel mapping, volume storage, resource limits, and progress tracking.

output_examples.input: I need a daily job that uses an API token and writes results.
output_examples.output: A scheduled job design with Modal secrets, a mounted volume, retry guidance, and logging recommendations.

best_practices: Use Modal Secrets for credentials and attach only the secrets each function needs.
Pin dependencies and choose GPU, CPU, memory, and timeout settings before scaling traffic.
Use volumes for persistent data and call commit after writes that other functions must read.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode production credentials in examples, source files, or image build steps.
Do not serve broad filesystem paths from web endpoints.
Do not scale to large GPU or container counts before testing cost and resource needs.

faq.question: Does this skill run Modal commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users decide when to install Modal, authenticate, run, or deploy.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with GPU workloads?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers GPU selection, CUDA-related setup, multi-GPU examples, and inference patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Modal Secrets, environment variables, and common credential patterns.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for Modal documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused assistant guide and should be checked against official Modal documentation.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits ML inference, batch processing, scheduled jobs, scientific computing, and serverless Python APIs.
